description: Mini program visual refresh PRD for turning the parent-facing WeChat mini program from a prototype-like utility into a polished, production-ready education product. The core goal is visual quality: pages should look intentional, trustworthy, calm, and finished. Button position and action arrangement are first-class requirements, especially on the parent home, bind, upload, wrongbook, progress, PDF, empty, loading, error, and success states.
scope: Only the WeChat mini program frontend under miniprogram/miniprogram/ is in product scope.
Main pages: parent-home, parent-bind, parent-upload, parent-wrongbook, shared parent API-facing UI states, and mini program page-level styles.
Tests and Ralph proof scripts may be updated when they directly guard mini program visual behavior.
nonGoals: Do not work on the website React frontend under frontend/.
Do not change bridge or website backend behavior unless a story explicitly identifies a visual-only contract gap and the user approves it.
Do not add new product features, new upload semantics, new AI box selection, or new backend APIs.
Do not redesign the business flow. Keep the existing parent flow: bind child, open home, upload wrong questions, check wrongbook/PDF.
Do not copy desktop admin dashboard layouts into the mini program. Use mobile-first mini program patterns.
Do not make purely decorative changes that hurt clarity, readability, or tap safety.
visualDirection: Warm, clean, trustworthy, parent-friendly, and workmanlike.
Use a restrained palette with clear primary action color, calm background, readable cards, and obvious status hierarchy.
Avoid childish decoration, dense developer-tool layout, oversized marketing hero sections, and one-note color themes.
Buttons must feel deliberately placed: one clear primary action per screen section, secondary actions nearby but visually quieter, destructive actions separated from primary flows.
globalRules: Read AGENTS.md, handoff.md, miniprogram/handoff.md, scripts/ralph/prd.json, and scripts/ralph/progress.txt before each story.
Work on exactly one user story per iteration.
Use the smallest possible edit that improves the requested visual surface.
Before editing any mini program file, read the current WXML/WXSS/JS/test content.
Every story must preserve existing upload, binding, wrongbook, PDF, task polling, and recovery behavior unless the story explicitly says otherwise.
Every story must add or update deterministic proof for visual/layout requirements. Prefer WXML/WXSS structural tests, page model tests, and mini program scope tests.
A story can only be marked passes=true after its focused proof and the relevant baseline proof pass.
After MP-VISUAL-001 lands, every later story must run scripts/ralph/miniprogram_visual_polish_proof.sh and scripts/ralph/miniprogram_upload_stability_proof.sh.
If a story touches upload UI, run the full upload stability proof too.
Commit each completed story separately after verification.
If proof fails, do not mark the story passes=true and do not commit.
experienceTargets: A parent opening the mini program should immediately feel this is a finished Starain/Xingrun product, not a prototype or internal test page.
Every screen should have a clear visual hierarchy: page title, context, primary content, primary action, secondary actions, and state feedback.
Button order should match the parent journey: choose or confirm child, select/take photo, add/adjust boxes, add optional reason, submit, check progress, open wrongbook/PDF.
Primary buttons must be easy to find and hard to confuse with secondary or destructive actions.
Action bars must stay stable on narrow phones and respect safe-area padding.
No important text or button may wrap awkwardly, overlap, become clipped, or jump position on small screens.
Empty, loading, failed, processing, partial success, and complete states should look designed, not like raw error messages.

userStories.title: Create mini program visual polish proof runner
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I need a single proof path for mini program visual polish so later Ralph iterations can guard button placement, page structure, and production-readiness without guessing.
acceptanceCriteria: Add scripts/ralph/miniprogram_visual_polish_proof.sh.
The proof must run mini program page structure/layout tests for parent-home, parent-bind, parent-upload, and parent-wrongbook.
The proof must include checks for primary action hierarchy, secondary action grouping, destructive action separation, bottom action/safe-area rules, and no obvious prototype-only wording.
The proof must not require WeChat devtools, a real device, production data, production secrets, Redis, RQ, or a running Flask server.
The proof output must make it obvious which visual contract failed.
Do not change mini program visual behavior in this story except to add tests or proof infrastructure.
Run the new visual proof through a temporary script and run scripts/ralph/miniprogram_upload_stability_proof.sh.
userStories.notes: Added scripts/ralph/miniprogram_visual_polish_proof.sh; proof covers parent-home, parent-bind, parent-upload, and parent-wrongbook visual structure/action hierarchy contracts without requiring WeChat devtools or services.

userStories.title: Define production mini program visual system
userStories.description: As a parent, I need the whole mini program to look like one finished product, with consistent colors, spacing, cards, typography, and controls.
acceptanceCriteria: Audit existing mini program WXML/WXSS for repeated page shells, card styles, button classes, spacing, status blocks, and prototype-like visual leftovers.
Introduce or normalize a small shared visual system for page background, cards, section headings, primary buttons, secondary buttons, icon buttons, state tags, and safe-area-aware bottom bars.
Keep the visual system mobile-first and compatible with WeChat mini program CSS constraints.
Do not make global style changes that break existing parent upload box/canvas interaction.
Add tests or scope checks that lock the shared visual primitives and prevent reintroducing scattered one-off primary button styles.
Run scripts/ralph/miniprogram_visual_polish_proof.sh and scripts/ralph/miniprogram_upload_stability_proof.sh.
userStories.notes: Shared mini program visual primitives now live in app.wxss for page shells, cards, headings, primary/secondary/icon buttons, state tags, and safe-area-aware bottom action bars. Page wxss no longer owns scattered primary/secondary button definitions; visual proof locks the shared system and upload baseline still passes.

userStories.title: Standardize button position and action hierarchy
userStories.description: As a parent, I need buttons to be placed where I expect them, with one obvious main action and no confusing or dangerous button arrangement.
acceptanceCriteria: Audit all parent-facing mini program pages for button order, grouping, labels, widths, sticky placement, tap safety, and destructive action placement.
Each major screen section must have at most one dominant primary action.
Secondary actions must be visually quieter and located near the content they affect.
Destructive actions such as deleting a box must be separated from primary submit/continue actions and must not sit in the easiest accidental tap location.
Upload page actions must follow the parent journey: photo/image input, box adjustment, optional reason, submit, progress/wrongbook.
Bottom submit/progress areas must be stable, safe-area-aware, and not cover important content.
Narrow-screen tests must prove buttons do not overlap, clip, jump, or wrap into awkward multi-line layouts.
Run scripts/ralph/miniprogram_visual_polish_proof.sh and scripts/ralph/miniprogram_upload_stability_proof.sh.
userStories.notes: Parent-facing action hierarchy is now standardized: child cards show upload as the primary action before wrongbook, upload box tools separate add/rotate from the danger delete action, success/progress next-step uses a primary wrongbook/progress button, and visual/upload proof scripts lock narrow-screen no-wrap and destructive separation.

userStories.title: Polish parent home into a finished entry screen
userStories.description: As a parent, I need the home screen to feel welcoming, organized, and immediately useful, with child cards and main actions arranged like a real product.
acceptanceCriteria: Refresh parent-home visual hierarchy: app identity, bound child context, primary child action, secondary bind/manage action, and status hints.
Child cards must look intentional and scan well with long child names, class names, and teacher names.
The primary action for each child must be obvious without creating a crowded button row.
The empty/no-child state must look designed and make binding the next obvious step.
Avoid marketing-style hero blocks; this is a utility home screen for repeat parent use.
Add or update tests that lock button placement, card structure, empty state, and narrow-screen behavior.
Run scripts/ralph/miniprogram_visual_polish_proof.sh and scripts/ralph/miniprogram_upload_stability_proof.sh.
userStories.notes: Parent home now uses Xingrun parent identity, designed empty state, bound-child count/context, child card class/teacher metadata, progress hint copy, and narrow-screen wrapping rules for long names and metadata.

userStories.title: Polish child binding page
userStories.description: As a parent binding a child, I need the page to feel simple, safe, and official, with form controls and confirmation actions clearly arranged.
acceptanceCriteria: Refresh parent-bind layout for page title, explanation, input/search area, result cards, already-bound child cards, and bind confirmation.
Primary bind action must be visually distinct and consistently placed inside the relevant child card or result block.
Already-bound and unavailable states must be readable without looking like raw debug output.
Long class/student/teacher names must wrap cleanly without pushing buttons into awkward positions.
Do not change binding API behavior or child identity matching.
Add or update tests that lock bind button hierarchy, card structure, empty/error states, and narrow-screen behavior.
Run scripts/ralph/miniprogram_visual_polish_proof.sh and scripts/ralph/miniprogram_upload_stability_proof.sh.
userStories.notes: Parent bind page now uses an official invite lookup panel, structured already-bound child cards, class result cards, per-student bind confirmation cards, a designed no-students state, and narrow-screen wrapping rules for long class/student text without changing binding APIs.

userStories.title: Polish wrong question upload page
userStories.description: As a parent uploading homework photos, I need the upload page to feel like a guided, polished tool instead of a prototype control panel.
acceptanceCriteria: Refresh parent-upload visual hierarchy for image input, selected image context, box tools, reason input, task stages, and final submit.
Keep existing manual box behavior, crop export behavior, task polling, recovery, and error semantics intact.
Photo/select-image actions, box actions, reason actions, and submit action must be visually separated into understandable groups.
The primary submit action must be stable, safe-area-aware, and easy to find after boxes are prepared.
Delete current box and rotate controls must be accessible but visually subordinate to submit.
Submitting/processing states must look designed and must not leave button areas in confusing positions.
Add or update tests that lock the upload action arrangement, bottom submit area, destructive action separation, status blocks, and narrow-screen behavior.
Run scripts/ralph/miniprogram_visual_polish_proof.sh and scripts/ralph/miniprogram_upload_stability_proof.sh.
userStories.notes: Parent upload page now has a guided visual flow for image input, selected image context, manual box tools, reason/topic entry, task progress, and a safe-area-aware submit panel. Existing crop/manual box/task polling behavior is unchanged; visual proof and upload stability proof passed through /tmp/xingrun_mp_visual_006_proof.sh.

userStories.title: Polish parent wrongbook and PDF entry
userStories.description: As a parent reviewing mistakes, I need the wrongbook page to feel like a child learning record, with cards, progress, and PDF actions arranged cleanly.
acceptanceCriteria: Refresh parent-wrongbook visual hierarchy for child identity, PDF entry, task progress, filters or topic controls if present, wrong question cards, and state feedback.
PDF action must be visible but not mistaken for the only path when records are still loading or processing.
Wrong question cards must separate topic/status/time/question preview/image/error information cleanly.
Failed, still-processing, PDF-not-ready, missing-PDF, download-failed, and open-failed states must look designed and recoverable.
Long LaTeX-preview text must wrap cleanly without breaking card or button layout.
Add or update tests that lock card hierarchy, PDF action placement, state blocks, and narrow-screen behavior.
Run scripts/ralph/miniprogram_visual_polish_proof.sh and scripts/ralph/miniprogram_upload_stability_proof.sh.
userStories.notes: Parent wrongbook now opens with a Xingrun wrongbook learning-record hero, separates upload progress, PDF status/action, topic filters, and wrong question cards, uses ghost styling for not-ready PDF actions, and locks designed loading/error/empty states plus card section hierarchy in visual proof.

userStories.title: Unify empty loading success error and processing states
userStories.description: As a parent, I need every non-happy-path state to look intentional and understandable, not like a raw technical placeholder.
acceptanceCriteria: Audit all parent-facing pages for empty, loading, success, partial success, processing, retryable failure, final failure, and unavailable states.
Unify state card layout, icon or marker treatment, title/body/action hierarchy, and retry/check-progress actions.
Parent-facing copy must be concise, calm, and action-oriented.
Low-level technical details may remain available only where already intentionally exposed for diagnostics; they must not dominate the visual hierarchy.
State actions must follow the same primary/secondary button rules as normal page actions.
Add or update tests that lock state component structure and prevent raw prototype placeholders.
Run scripts/ralph/miniprogram_visual_polish_proof.sh and scripts/ralph/miniprogram_upload_stability_proof.sh.
userStories.notes: Unified parent-facing non-happy-path state anatomy across home, bind, upload, and wrongbook: shared state markers now cover loading, empty, processing, success, and error states; upload progress/result and wrongbook upload/item recognition states use marker + title/body structure; home error now has a retry action. Visual and upload stability proofs passed through /tmp/xingrun_mp_visual_008_proof.sh.

userStories.title: Harden narrow screen and WeChat runtime layout
userStories.description: As a parent on small iPhone, Android, or HarmonyOS WeChat containers, I need every page to remain readable, tap-safe, and visually stable.
acceptanceCriteria: Add or extend structural tests for narrow-screen class rules on parent-home, parent-bind, parent-upload, and parent-wrongbook.
No primary button may rely on a fixed width that risks clipping common Chinese labels.
Button text must not be hidden, clipped, or forced into awkward multi-line layouts.
Sticky or bottom action areas must reserve enough content padding and safe-area spacing.
Cards must not depend on side-by-side layouts that collapse badly on narrow screens.
Document remaining manual checks for WeChat devtools and real devices in scripts/ralph/progress.txt without marking them as automated proof.
Run scripts/ralph/miniprogram_visual_polish_proof.sh and scripts/ralph/miniprogram_upload_stability_proof.sh.
userStories.notes: Added WeChat narrow-runtime guardrails and structural proof coverage: shared parent page shells now cap width at 100vw, hide horizontal overflow, reserve page bottom safe-area padding with constant/env fallbacks, keep shared button primitives min-width 0/max-width 100%/text-overflow clip, and upload bottom actions include constant/env safe-area padding. Visual and upload stability proofs passed through /tmp/xingrun_mp_visual_009_proof.sh.

userStories.title: Add final mini program visual acceptance guardrail
userStories.description: As the product owner, I need one final guardrail that proves the mini program visual refresh has a finished-product feel and preserved existing upload behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: Add a final local acceptance proof or checklist script for the visual refresh.
The final proof must verify every story in this PRD is passes=true before reporting complete.
The proof must verify parent-home, parent-bind, parent-upload, and parent-wrongbook all use the agreed visual system and action hierarchy.
The proof must verify button placement contracts: one primary action per section, secondary grouping, destructive separation, bottom action/safe-area rules, and narrow-screen constraints.
The proof must verify no active mini program page presents itself as a prototype, demo, temporary, debug, or internal test UI.
The proof must verify the story did not modify website frontend or backend files unless explicitly allowed by the PRD.
Update scripts/ralph/progress.txt with final status and remaining manual WeChat devtools/real-device visual smoke checks.
Run scripts/ralph/miniprogram_visual_polish_proof.sh and scripts/ralph/miniprogram_upload_stability_proof.sh.
